A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Generate Any Scene and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across versions, including v3 Appendix G, which becomes Appendix I in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on self-improvement, targeted distillation, reinforcement learning, generated-content detection, and visual-generation evaluation, including appendix ablations and a human study.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds quality/diversity measurements, unseen-composition evaluation, a Gemini scene-graph comparison, and a gender-bias evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix D.1 changes the stated hard-concept selection criterion from average VQA Score to average TIFA Score, a limited revision to the distillation selection rule. However, D.2 retains the VQA description, leaving the implemented criterion unresolved. The five-stage engine and other training frameworks are retained; expanded filtering and image-selection descriptions do not establish additional method changes.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on unseen combinations of familiar elements, DALL-Eval gender-related prompts after fine-tuning, and direct scene-graph generation tests covering vocabulary distribution and structural validity. These extend the evaluated scenarios beyond v3's visual-generation benchmarks and taxonomy-based fairness analysis.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds Gemini 2.5-flash as an evaluated alternative scene-graph generator in Tables 20–22. This introduces a direct comparison against LLM-based data generation, a substantive comparison category absent from v3. Earlier visual-model, real-caption, web-image, and reward-source comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 400-caption test excluding previously seen combinations, additional CLIPScore/ImageReward/LPIPS evaluation on GenAI-Bench, and DALL-Eval gender MAD measurement. Appendix G evaluates 10K graphs, with Gemini receiving batches of 20 graphs using randomly sampled 5% metadata subsets and 3–12 elements. Existing training budgets are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds analyses of generation diversity, generalization to unseen compositions, gender bias introduced by fine-tuning, and scene-graph errors such as missing fields and hallucinated elements. These address additional robustness and failure questions. The earlier paraphrasing, human-alignment, full-fine-tuning, reward, and detector analyses remain.

E5.justification: There is no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting. Existing human-study counts and correlation reporting are retained. New Gini, entropy, LPIPS, and MAD scores are evaluation measurements; the disclosed four-image selection procedure is not statistical replication.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and 20–23 add substantial results while earlier benchmark scores are retained. Table 3 reports GAS-FT VQAScore 0.6109 versus CC3M-FT 0.6044, but ImageReward is -0.2497 versus 0.2602 and the base model's 0.4861. Table 21 reports 100% structurally valid graphs for GAS versus 49.1% for Gemini. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v3 under matched conditions.

T1.justification: The scene-graph representation and mathematical content are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear. Appendix G's statements about structural guarantees are conceptual and empirical rather than new formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same data-engine contribution and four applications. The headline claims of approximately 4% self-improvement, 10% distillation improvement, and +5% over CLIP-based rewards remain unchanged in meaning.

C2.justification: Appendices G–H add substantive arguments about advantages over LLM generation, useful unrealistic scenes versus nonsensical scenes, and mechanisms limiting social-bias propagation. Section 3 adds interpretations concerning quality, diversity, and combinatorial generalization. Its claim of highest ImageReward on unseen compositions contradicts Table 3. The original limitations are retained through relocation.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses generating four images per targeted caption and selecting the highest-VQA image. H.1 details optional filtering through LAION frequencies, embedding-based top-k compatibility, and Vera/perplexity thresholds. Section 4 corrects 100 concepts to the 81 already listed in v3's appendix. Existing training/hardware details and code/data links are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds the DALL-Eval reference by Cho, Zala, and Bansal and expands the existing positioning against LLM-based caption generation in Appendix G. Other cited works are retained after matching reordered references and changed year suffixes; the related-work section's scope is stable.

P1.justification: v4 makes local language and affiliation corrections, adds conference headers, changes citation formatting and bibliography ordering, and expands Sections 3–4. New Appendices G–H precede the unchanged limitations, now Appendix I. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds paired main-text Tables 2–3 and appendix Tables 20–23, improves Figure 1's rendering, and relocates existing figures during text reflow. Existing plots and qualitative examples are retained. These are localized display additions and refinements within the established layout.

improvement.justification: The direct Gemini comparison supplies evidence for engine advantages previously argued largely conceptually, while the unseen-composition, diversity, and bias checks strengthen validation. Clearer filtering documentation also helps assessment. These benefits are tempered by the contradicted ImageReward claim in Table 3 and the inconsistent TIFA/VQA selection descriptions in D.1–D.2. The net gain is useful but limited relative to v3's already extensive evidence.
